devi_anga: Tongue of Sati in the Shakti Peetha tradition
mythology: The Ashtadasha tradition names the Devi here Vaishnavi. At Jawala Ji the natural flames are revered as the fiery manifestation of Sati’s tongue.
pilgrimage_significance: Devotees have darshan of the nine named Jyotis in a shared flame pit. The Shaiyan Aarti continues at the adjacent Seja Bhawan.
historical_notes: The main hillside compound follows the photo and satellite layout. Shri Jawala Ji and Seja Bhawan have distinct gilded roofs around the chequered court. The Charan Paduka and domed pavilions stand in the courtyard. The raised Gorakh Dibbi terrace connects to the adjoining Radha–Krishna and Shiva–Shakti shrines.
